title: Probing Speaker Identity Sensitivity in Audio Deepfake Detectors
abstract: arXiv:2607.21820v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Audio deepfake detectors are trained to distinguish genuine speech from synthetic speech and often perform well on standard benchmarks. Yet the same detector that achieves less than 1% error on one dataset can see its error rate increase twentyfold when evaluated on a different dataset. We argue that one contributing factor is speaker-identity reliance: standard training corpora correlate speaker identity with the genuine/synthetic label, allowing detectors to partially rely on speaker-related cues rather than synthesis artifacts alone. We propose the Identity Sensitivity Score (ISS), a per-utterance diagnostic that quantifies how much a detector's output changes across different speaker identity contexts. ISS requires no ground-truth labels at inference time and can be computed from the detector score and a pool of reference speaker examples. translated_title: 探测音频深度伪造检测器中的说话人身份敏感性
translated_abstract: 音频深度伪造检测器旨在区分真实语音与合成语音，并且在标准基准测试中通常表现良好。然而，同一个在某个数据集上错误率低于1%的检测器，在不同数据集上评估时，其错误率可能会增加二十倍。我们认为，造成这一现象的一个因素是说话人身份依赖性：标准训练语料库将说话人身份与真实/合成标签相关联，使检测器能够部分依赖与说话人相关的线索，而非仅仅依赖合成痕迹。我们提出了身份敏感性分数（Identity Sensitivity Score, ISS），这是一种逐条语音的诊断指标，用于量化检测器的输出在不同说话人身份情境下的变化程度。ISS在推理时无需真实标签，只需利用检测器的分数和一组参考说话人样本即可计算。在两个检测器和两个数据集上的实验表明，被错误分类的语音样本的ISS分数……
tldr: 论文提出身份敏感性分数（ISS）这一新型诊断指标，揭示音频深度伪造检测器的跨数据集性能下降部分源于检测器依赖说话人身份线索而非真正的合成痕迹。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Identity Sensitivity Score (ISS), a diagnostic metric showing that the cross-dataset performance drop of audio deepfake detectors partly stems from their reliance on speaker identity cues rather than synthesis artifacts alone.
